stem:
In one office, this statement is true:
Some engineers are choir members.

Based only on this statement, which must also be true?
choices: Some engineers are not choir members.
hints: In logic, "some" means "at least one". It says nothing about the rest of the group.
Draw an engineers circle and a choir circle that overlap. Put at least one person in the overlap.
Read the overlap from both sides: the person there belongs to both groups. Then, for each other choice, try to draw a picture where the statement is true but the choice is false.

solution.methodName: Draw circles, then look for a counterexample

steps.action: "Some engineers are choir members" means at least one person is both an engineer and a choir member. Draw two overlapping circles and put that person, call her Joy, in the overlap.
steps.why: "Some" only promises at least one. It could be one person, a few, or even all of them.

steps.action: Joy is a choir member, and Joy is an engineer. So at least one choir member is an engineer: "Some choir members are engineers" must be true.
steps.why: The overlap belongs to both circles, so you can read it starting from either group.

steps.action: "Some engineers are not choir members" does not have to be true: if every engineer in the office sings in the choir, the statement is still true.
steps.why: "Some are" does not mean "some are not." The statement says nothing about engineers outside the choir.

steps.action: "All choir members are engineers" does not have to be true: a choir member who is an accountant keeps the statement true.
"No engineers are choir members" is false, because Joy is both.
The answer is "Some choir members are engineers."

"Some are" does not mean "some are not." Counterexample: every engineer in the office is in the choir. The statement is still true, but this choice is false.
This turns one overlap into a whole circle. Counterexample: the choir also has an accountant who is not an engineer. The statement is still true, but this choice is false.
This goes against the statement. At least one engineer is a choir member, so this is false.
